questions.question: Are AutoSpotting and Karpenter direct competitors?
questions.answer: Not exactly. Karpenter is a Kubernetes-native node provisioner that watches pending pods and launches right-sized nodes, and it can request Spot capacity directly. AutoSpotting works one layer down, at the EC2 AutoScaling group, and converts existing group capacity to Spot with automatic on-demand fallback. They operate at different layers and can suit different situations.

questions.question: When does Karpenter make more sense?
questions.answer: Karpenter fits when you want a Kubernetes-native provisioner, you are replacing Cluster Autoscaler, and you want node consolidation and bin-packing driven by pending pods. It replaces your provisioning model, which you then define and operate through NodePools.

questions.question: When does AutoSpotting make more sense?
questions.answer: AutoSpotting fits when your nodes run on managed or self-managed node groups you do not want to replace, when you want Spot with automatic on-demand fallback without adopting a new provisioner, and when you also run non-Kubernetes services on AutoScaling groups, such as ECS, Elastic Beanstalk, or plain ASGs, and want one approach across all of them.

questions.question: Can I use both?
questions.answer: Yes. Karpenter can manage the Kubernetes clusters where you want a native provisioner, while AutoSpotting brings Spot with on-demand fallback to the AutoScaling groups behind your other clusters and non-Kubernetes services. Choose per workload rather than treating it as a single either-or decision.
